[00:08] 3939349109241760902: hey, thanks for making the time. can you hear me okay?

[01:17] 1913880516720761693: sure. so we're Vitalsync, we're in the healthtech space. and yeah, we had a really bad outage last month that made it to the exec team, so now there's budget.
[01:55] 1913880516720761693: we're locked into an annual contract that auto-renews and it's a fight to get out.
[03:13] 3939349109241760902: that's a really common story. what are you using today?

[05:02] 1913880516720761693: we've also looked at Grafalt and Splunkr a bit.
[06:15] 3939349109241760902: got it. and is that something you're actively trying to fix?
[06:38] 1913880516720761693: we've basically decided we're leaving our current vendor, the question is just who we go to next.
[07:46] 3939349109241760902: got it. and is that something you're actively trying to fix?
[08:46] 1913880516720761693: we've got like 80 microservices now and no real tracing, so debugging cross-service issues is guesswork.
[09:36] 1913880516720761693: our monitoring bill is now our second biggest cloud line item and it's totally unpredictable.
[10:24] 3939349109241760902: makes sense. when you picture this working well, what does that look like?
[11:18] 1913880516720761693: the fact that setup is supposedly quick matters a lot to us, we don't have spare cycles.
[11:38] 3939349109241760902: and what would hold you back from moving on this?
[11:58] 1913880516720761693: my worry is migration, we've got years of dashboards and runbooks built on the current tool.
[12:19] 1913880516720761693: everyone's trained on the existing dashboards, there's a lot of muscle memory.
[12:55] 3939349109241760902: totally fair. let me show you how a couple of teams like yours handled exactly that.
[13:23] 1913880516720761693: yeah that'd be helpful. timeline-wise we'd want to move fast.
[14:36] 3939349109241760902: great — here's what I'd suggest as a next step.
[15:00] 1913880516720761693: works for me.
